excerpts: Mutual TLS authentication requires two-way authentication between the client and the server.

By default, clients can invoke your API by using the execute-api endpoint that API Gateway generates for your API. To ensure that clients can access your API only by using a custom domain name with mutual TLS, disable the default execute-api endpoint.
To enable mutual TLS for a REST API, you must configure a custom domain name for your API.
Note: Mutual TLS isn't supported for private APIs.
API Gateway doesn't verify if a certificate has been revoked.
API Gateway forwards the certificates that clients provide to Lambda authorizers and to backend integrations.
To configure mutual TLS you need: A custom domain name, at least one certificate configured in AWS Certificate Manager, a truststore configured and uploaded to Amazon S3.
Note: Mutual TLS isn't supported for private APIs.
API Gateway doesn't verify if a certificate has been revoked.
A private API is a REST API that is only callable from within an Amazon VPC.
Only REST APIs are supported.
Private APIs only support TLS 1.2.
Add aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce conditions to your API's resource policy to restrict access.
If you map a custom domain name to a WebSocket API, you can't map it to a REST API or an HTTP API.
Only Regional custom domain names are supported.
For the minimum TLS version, only TLS 1.2 is supported.

excerpts: You can only use a Lambda authorizer function for the $connect route.
Changing authorizer in $connect doesn't affect the already connected client.
There is no standard mechanism to differentiate JWT access tokens from other types of JWTs, such as OpenID Connect ID tokens.
Currently, only RSA-based algorithms are supported.
API Gateway caches the public key for up to two hours on a best-effort basis.
aud or client_id – Must match one of the audience entries that is configured for the authorizer.
scope or scp – The token must include at least one of the scopes in the route's authorizationScopes.

You can enable caching for a Lambda authorizer by specifying an authorizerResultTtlInSeconds. When caching is enabled for an authorizer, API Gateway uses the authorizer's identity sources as the cache key.

excerpts: Mutual TLS passthrough: The load balancer sends the entire client certificate chain to the target, without verifying it.
Mutual TLS verify: The load balancer performs X.509 client certificate authentication for clients.
The load balancer passes the client certificate information to the backend using HTTP headers.
Session resumption is not supported while using mutual TLS passthrough or verify modes.
The token endpoint supports client_secret_basic and client_secret_post authentication.

excerpts: iss: Your application's Client ID.
sub: Your application's Client ID.
aud: The URL of the Auth0 tenant or custom domain that receives the assertion.
The client assertion is a one-time use token, and we recommend the shortest possible expiry time. Auth0 supports a maximum of 5 minutes for the lifetime of a token.
jti: A unique claim ID created by the client.
The maximum length of the JWT assertion is 2048 bytes.
private_key_jwt: Use this when you want maximum security. This method is more complex and requires a server, so it can't be used with public clients.
The private key that you use to sign the JWT must have the corresponding public key registered in the client's JWKSet.
If jti is specified, the token can only be used once.
The exp claim fails the request if the expiration time is more than one hour in the future or has already expired.
self_signed_tls_client_auth ... mTLS client authentication is a self-service Early Access (EA) feature.
The token's cnf claim contains an x5t#S256 member with the certificate's base64url-encoded SHA-256 thumbprint.
Client authentication with Signed JWT — This is based on the RFC7523 specification.
During authentication, the client generates a JWT token and signs it with its private key and sends it to Keycloak in the particular request in the client_assertion parameter.
Configure the JWKS URL where Keycloak can download the client's public keys.
For the provider URL: Use https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
For the Audience: Use sts.amazonaws.com
token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/octo-branch
If you use a workflow with an environment, the sub field must reference the environment name: repo:ORG-NAME/REPO-NAME:environment:ENVIRONMENT-NAME
For repositories created after July 15, 2026, or that have opted in to immutable subject claims, the sub claim includes immutable owner and repository IDs
The job or workflow run requires a permissions setting with id-token: write
This backend also supports state locking which can be enabled by setting the use_lockfile argument to true.
It is highly recommended that you enable Bucket Versioning on the S3 bucket to allow for state recovery.
Locking can be enabled via S3 or DynamoDB. However, DynamoDB-based locking is deprecated and will be removed in a future minor version.
If use_lockfile is set, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:DeleteObject are required on the lock file, e.g., arn:aws:s3:::mybucket/path/to/my/key.tflock.
